body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/discussions/11172
Originally posted by **pdmnyberg** March 19, 2024 I have a system where I would like to filter the sub-items of the items I would like to return in the main query. The way I am doing this can be expressed using the `pytest` below. My problem is that I am getting different results when I update from version `2.0.27` to `2.0.28`. I have only encountered the problem using postres, while sqlite seems to work fine. Is this a new expected behavior? Am I doing something wrong in this query or the session setup? ## Broken requirements: ``` pytest sqlalchemy==2.0.28 psycopg2-binary==2.9.9 ``` ## Working requirements: ``` pytest sqlalchemy==2.0.27 psycopg2-binary==2.9.9 ``` ## The test The following script expects a working postgres database and can be run as follows: ```bash DB_HOST="db-host" \ DB_USER="db-user" \ DB_PASSWORD="db-password" \ DB_DATABASE="db-database" \ pytest test_sql_search.py ``` ```python import os from sqlalchemy import ( Column, Integer, String, ForeignKey, ) from sqlalchemy.orm import relationship, declarative_base from sqlalchemy import create_engine from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker from sqlalchemy.orm import subqueryload Base = declarative_base() class SubItem(Base): __tablename__ = "sub_items" id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True, autoincrement=True) item_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey('items.id', ondelete="CASCADE")) name = Column(String) number = Column(Integer) class Item(Base): __tablename__ = "items" id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True, autoincrement=True) name = Column(String) number = Column(Integer) sub_items = relationship( 'SubItem', backref='item', cascade="all, delete-orphan" ) def create_session(): DB_HOST = os.getenv("DB_HOST") DB_USER = os.getenv("DB_USER") DB_PASSWORD = os.getenv("DB_PASSWORD") DB_DATABASE = os.getenv("DB_DATABASE") assert DB_HOST is not None, "database host must be set" assert DB_USER is not None, "database user must be set" assert DB_PASSWORD is not None, "database password must be set" assert DB_DATABASE is not None, "database must be set" engine = create_engine( f"postgresql://{DB_USER}:{DB_PASSWORD}@{DB_HOST}/{DB_DATABASE}" ) Base.metadata.drop_all(bind=engine) Base.metadata.create_all(bind=engine) return sessionmaker(bind=engine) def test_create_items(): SessionLocal = create_session() number_of_items = 200 number_of_sub_items = 20 sub_item_numbers = list(range(number_of_sub_items)) with SessionLocal() as db: items = [ Item(name=f"Item:{i}", number=i) for i in range(number_of_items) ] for item in items: db.add(item) db.commit() for item in items: item.sub_items = [ SubItem(name=f"SubItem:{item.id}:{i}", number=i) for i in range(number_of_sub_items) ] db.commit() with SessionLocal() as db: base_query = db.query(Item) result_items = list(base_query) assert len(items) == number_of_items, ( f"all items are created {number_of_items}" ) for item in result_items: result_sub_items = list(item.sub_items) assert len(result_sub_items) == number_of_sub_items, ( f"all sub items for item are created {number_of_sub_items}" ) for sub_item_number in sub_item_numbers: with SessionLocal() as db: print(sub_item_number) base_query = db.query(Item) sub_item_query = Item.sub_items base_query = base_query.filter( Item.number > 50, Item.number <= 100 ) sub_item_query = sub_item_query.and_( SubItem.number == sub_item_number ) base_query = base_query.options( subqueryload(sub_item_query), ) items = list(base_query) assert len(items) == 50, "the number of items should be 50" for item in items: sub_items = list(item.sub_items) assert len(sub_items) == 1, "one item should be selected" for sub_item in sub_items: assert sub_item.number == sub_item_number, ( "the queried number should be the resulting number" ) ```
